title: Capacity regression playbook and remediation runbook for Dedicated fleets
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Summary: After a production incident on 2025-02-14 we observed a sustained throughput regression in multiple Dedicated customer fleets causing increased tail latency and token-cost surges. This ticket captures the incident summary, root cause analysis, immediate mitigations, and a concrete runbook + action items to prevent recurrence. Goal: provide an on-call-friendly playbook that reduces MTTI and ensures safe autoscaler rollbacks, traffic steering, and configuration gating for Dedicated capacity. Scope: dedicated GPU pools, fleet autoscaler, routing policies, and compile-time kernel selection logic. Out of scope: hosted API control-plane changes and unrelated infra alerts.
incident_summary: On 2025-02-14 02:30 UTC a regression in the autoscaler + kernel selection path caused several Dedicated fleets to under-provision for typical request mix. Symptoms: sudden drop in throughput, KV cache miss spike, UPSCALE events failing due to a cap in API rate limiter for scaling commands, and increased token latency from 30-70ms to 150-400ms per token across impacted fleets. ~12 customers experienced degraded SLAs; 3 customers hit their internal error budgets and escalated to support.

root_cause: Regression introduced in runtime-1.21: heuristic intended to prefer low-latency kernels for short sequences inadvertently flagged production workloads as 'small batch' leading to suboptimal kernel selection and ~40% throughput drop for common production seq-lengths.

Autoscaler change in dedicated-controller v3.4 introduced a backoff/rate-limit when multiple concurrent scale operations are attempted. Combined with aggressive canary pushes, this created a window where planned scale-ups were not executed.
Monitoring coverage gap: no synthetic end-to-end throughput tests for the 1-4s prefix KV-cache heavy traffic patterns used by several enterprise customers.
Runbook gaps: on-call escalation flow did not include immediate guidance to disable kernel-selection heuristics; operator acted manually after consulting runtime team.
Insufficient CI gating on the autoscaler rate-limiter interaction; staging tests did not mimic concurrent multi-fleet scale scenario.
A misconfigured feature flag rollout allowed the kernel heuristic to reach 30% of Dedicated fleets before perf signals were visible.
immediate_mitigations: Reverted kernel-selection heuristic flag for Dedicated fleets (flag: runtime.kernel_heuristic_v2) to 0% within 20 minutes of detection
Temporary emergency scaling overrides issued to critical customer fleets to ensure throughput targets were met
Raised autoscaler operation rate-limit threshold for Dedicated controller and added temporary exception for scale requests tagged 'incident-override'
Routed non-private customers to healthy regions where capacity was available using smart-routing rules
Customer comms: sent targeted status updates to affected accounts and opened priority support tickets for escalations
monitoring_and_alerting_changes: Add synthetic throughput canary that exercises typical enterprise prompt shapes (prefix-heavy KV cache + 1-4s decoding) every 5 minutes
Create alert when autoscaler scale requests receive >1% 429 responses over a 5-minute window
Add a dashboard widget showing kernel-selection distribution and per-kernel P50/P95 latency for Dedicated fleets
Add a SLA degradation signal tied to both absolute token latency and percent of scale requests delayed > 60s
runbook_steps: Step 1: Verify alert and scope affected fleets using dashboard 'Dedicated fleet health'
Step 2: If scale requests are failing with 429, check dedicated-controller logs for rate-limiter hits; escalate to control-plane on-call
Step 3: If throughput regression correlates with kernel-selection drift, disable runtime.kernel_heuristic_v2 flag for impacted fleets and force a warm restart of runtime processes
Step 4: If immediate scale needed, use emergency override to set fleet target count and confirm worker spin-up in the infra dashboard
Step 5: For private deployments where remote flag flips are unavailable, instruct customer operator with atomic steps to revert the kernel heuristic via the private admin script (link in docs)
Step 6: Notify customers and internal stakeholders with templated status update; log incident timeline in PagerDuty incident
Step 7: After mitigation, monitor synthetic canaries and kernel distribution for 2 hours before closing incident

acceptance_criteria: Synthetic canary is running every 5 minutes and failures generate an alert
New CI test added and passing on PRs that touch autoscaler or rate-limiter code paths

Runbook updated and published; two on-call engineers sign off on clarity and steps
Audit log for incident-override scale requests available in Console
risks_and_tradeoffs: Slower rollout cadence for kernel heuristics may delay performance wins for some low-latency workloads
Temporary relax of autoscaler rate limits during incidents increases risk of control-plane saturation if abused; must be coupled with strong auditing
Adding synthetic canaries increases monitoring cost and false-positive surface; threshold tuning required

postmortem_notes: Key learning: intersection failures (kernel selection + autoscaler rate limits) are high-risk. Engineering recommendation is to treat kernel-selection heuristics as runtime-level performance features that must be gated by production canaries and CI concurrency tests. Also: ensure Dedicated controller has a documented emergency override path with auditability.
next_steps: Assign each action item to owner and confirm schedule on next weekly reliability sync. Ship hotfix for autoscaler backoff and land feature-flag guardrails before the next runtime canary. Run a cross-team tabletop within two weeks. Update customer-facing KB with incident summary and mitigation guidance.
